newsitem.title: UK: GOLF-LEONARD NOT SURPRISED BY TITLE CHALLENGE.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-LEONARD NOT SURPRISED BY TITLE CHALLENGE.

text.p: American Justin Leonard is one of the few people not surprised to see his name second on the leader board at the halfway stage of the British Open.

"I don't know that I'm surprised," said the former U.S. amateur champion. "Very pleased, but not really surprised," he said after shooting a joint lowest of the day 66 for a two round total of 135 -- two strokes behind Briton Darren Clarke.
"I've been playing well and since I got here Sunday I feel I've got to know the course very well. I've been able to prepare.
"I felt very good on Thursday morning when I woke up, confident about my game and the golf course."
He is in his fourth year as a professional and has risen rapidly up the rankings. He won the Kemper Open last month for his second U.S. Tour victory after taking the Buick Open last year.
Starting the day two-under-par, Leonard blasted his way into contention over the first seven holes with two eagles, two birdies and just one dropped shot.
The eagles came on long par fives and Leonard put them down to a new driver which he said had given him an extra 10 to 20 yards off the tee.

"The driver is great. It has taken a lot of pressure off some of the other areas of my game," he said. "I don't think with the driver I was using I would have been able to hit a five-iron on to those greens. It has made a big difference."
Leonard has played in three previous British Opens, twice after having to qualify, and has enjoyed them all.
"This is a tournament I look forward to playing," he said. "You have to hit so many different types of shot here. I think the greens are such a challenge because there are so many different options."

After Thursday's high winds had made the course difficult Leonard woke to much sunnier, gentle conditions on Friday. He also got out of bed to find that Clarke, in one of the early groups, had already stormed away from the field with a 66.

But he said he did not feel under pressure. "I wanted to go out and hit the ball solid and give myself some chances. Obviously eagling the par fives got me off to a good start. Then I said: 'Now we are going to milk these conditions".
